_about: The rules of the Referee: written by the adults before the session, shown to the young people as the frame of their experiment, never changed during the session, never by a personality. The Referee applies them to every command, with caution: sideways and backwards, where the robot does not see, a cell that could hold a card counts as holding one; forwards, the robot stops in front of a card by itself, so a card seen from far blocks nothing. The time a move may take is in mat.json, with the mat; limits on the robot's counters are optional, below. Values of the simulator; on the real robot TO BE COMPLETED.
_limits: Optional limits on the robot's counters, per mission (per session without a mission): "moves" (a step, a slide or a quarter turn; look_around counts one), "commands" (what the Referee sends that acts: MOVE, TURN, HOLD, STOP, LED), "cells" (the cells the robot really went through). None by default: what costs is the calls to the model, limited by the Strategist (turns, dollars per mission). Example: {"moves": 40}.
_start: Where the robot starts its mission: {"cell": "A6", "facing": "north"}; only the way it faces, {"facing": "north"} (it starts facing the top of the mat, on a cell nobody gives), or only its cell, {"cell": "A6"}; null for the start of mat.json; "unknown" when nobody says where it stands: the Cartographer then works relative to where it started, and finds its place on the mat with the border (the distance sensor sees it) and the landmarks.
_mat_north_up: The mat lies with north at the top: the robot's compass (magnetometer) gives the way it faces, so the Cartographer only looks for the cell.
_landmarks: Cards the adults put on a known cell before the session, {"fire-station": "A6"}: when the camera recognises one, the Cartographer knows better where the robot is. Useful when boxes hide the border, or without the compass (the border alone leaves two places on a mat that looks the same turned round).
